title: Fresh Horseradish Cream Sauce
headnote: Standalone creamy horseradish spread from June 14, 2026 conversation; made for Roast Beef, Swiss & Horseradish Ciabatta. The discussed quantities were 2 tbsp freshly grated horseradish, ¼ cup sour cream, 1 tsp Dijon, and a pinch of salt. Approximate gram equivalents below; exact amount of vinegar for this small sauce batch was not recorded.

ingredientGroups.title: Sauce
items: 12–15 g freshly grated horseradish root (original: 2 tbsp; approximate)
60 g sour cream (original: ¼ cup; approximate)
A few drops of white vinegar, optional, to fix the horseradish heat after grating

steps: Peel the fresh horseradish root and finely grate 2 tablespoons in a well-ventilated area; avoid leaning over the freshly grated root.

For more pronounced heat, allow the fresh grated horseradish to stand about 1–3 minutes, then add a few drops of vinegar if desired to stabilize the pungency. This vinegar amount is a practical small-batch suggestion, not a recovered exact historical measurement.
Mix the grated horseradish with sour cream, Dijon mustard, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Taste and adjust salt or horseradish. Refrigerate until ready to serve, then spread generously onto ciabatta with roast beef and Swiss.
